answer: Random peer audit blocks fake identities. A newcomer posts a 20-unit deposit, pays a 5-unit fee, and files a record signed with a quill. Three random auditors check it for a closed loop of contacts, like a vine around one trunk. Failure burns the deposit; a pass faces a 30% draw. Making 1,000 fakes costs 25,000 units for at most 10,000 reward, a 15,000 loss. A zephyr cannot hide fakes here: honest agents pay one fee and keep undiluted rewards.
